preview: Atharva Tarlekar shares his interview experience for a Full-Time Employee (FTE) role at Deutsche Bank, detailing the 5-round hiring process including online assessment, technical rounds, professional fitness, and HR interview.
content: Deutsche Bank Name: Atharva Tarlekar Branch: CS Eligibility Criteria: Branch: CS,IT,EXTC CPI: 7 No Backlogs Hiring Workflow There were a total of 5 rounds: 1. Online Assessment 2. Technical Interview 1 (Offline) 3. Technical Interview 2 (Offline) 4. Professional Fitness (Offline) 5. HR Interview (Offline) 1. Online Assessment Hackerearth was the platform used for the online evaluation. Three coding questions were included in the test. 1. Power Limit Difficulty: Easy Topic: No specific topic. We are given powers of 2 resources A & B. To execute the software, you must choose one resource from a possible two resources each second. The resource power should be larger than 1 at the moment of choosing. The strength of the chosen resource is reduced by two each second, while the power of the unselected resource is increased by one. When at least one resource is powered down, the programme terminates. Determine how long your software can run for if you choose your resources wisely. Input: int A,B Output: Maximum time for which software runs. Function to Complete: int PowerLimit(int A, int B) { } Approach: For every iteration the power of a resource which is used is decremented by 2 and the power of the unused resource is incremented by 1, hence to run it for maximum amount of time we need to choose the resource having the greater power until any of the resource is depleted. Solution Verdict: All Test cases passed. 2. Auto suggest Difficulty: Medium Topic: DP We are given a vector of strings containing N words and a query word S. We need to auto-suggest the best word from the vector that is closest to S. For comparing the distance between the word from the vector and the query word S we are given a parameter called Levenshtein distance. And if two words have the same Levenshtein distance, then priority is given to the Lexicographically smaller word. Levenshtein Distance is defined as the minimum number of edits required to convert one string to the other. Operations allowed for the edit are insertions,deletions,replacement. Exactly similar to Edit Distance (LeetCode) https://leetcode.com/problems/edit-distance/ Input: vector<string> words string S Output: Closest word from the vector words. Function to Complete: string solve(vector<string> words, string S) { } Approach: This was a straightforward question for me because I had already solved the edit distance problem from leetcode previously. So I just called the editDistance function for every word from the given vector. The word which returns the least distance is our answer. Solution Verdict: All Test cases passed. 3. Backlink Sorting Difficulty: Medium Topic: Customized sorting We are given a vector of strings containing titles of N web pages and a vector of backlinks for each web page. Our task is to sort the web pages in descending order of number of backlinks. Also, If 2 web pages had equal number of backlinks, keep them in their original order. Note: Backlinks are the links from other web pages to a web page. Input: vector<string> webPage vector<int> backlinks Output: Backlink sorted vector of titles of web pages. Function to Complete: vector<string> Sorter(vector<string> webPage, vector<int> Backlinks) { } Approach: I created a new vector<pair<string,int>> vec and stored the {title,backlink} in the vector for every web page. Now, I created a comparator to sort the “vec” as per the given condition. Solution Verdict: All Test cases passed. NOTE: There were a total of 4 rounds, and they were all extremely lengthy, so before moving on to the tech rounds, I could miss a few questions. Apologies!! 2. Technical Interview 1 [1 hour] Difficulty: Medium The interviewer was very friendly and she made sure that I’m relaxed before beginning the interview.The obligatory "introduce yourself" question kicked off the interview. I discussed my education, internship, side projects, and tech stack in that sequence. She asked about the internship at the beginning of the interview because I completed my internship as a research intern in VJTI itself, and I responded by outlining the full process of my work. I was quite thorough with my explanation and she looked satisfied with my answer. I was asked a series of questions containing almost everything like DSA, OOPS, DBMS, OS, Puzzles, and real life examples. 1. You are given a binary array separate the 0’s and 1’s. My Answer: Obviously, it is the easiest question you’ve seen so far isn't it. I counted numbers of 0’s and 1’s and created 2 arrays and just stored 0’s and 1’s in them. Now, she asked me to optimize this, so I said O(n) is already an optimal solution and if you want to optimize it further you can do it in O(n/2) by 2 pointer approach to sort the array in-place. She was satisfied with the approach. 2. She asked me if I know A* algorithm? My Answer: I was aware about what the algorithm does but I didn't know the total algorithm. She didn't expect me to explain the entire algorithm either. So, I just told the goal of the algorithm and she moved onto the next question. (PS- The algorithm is in our syllabus Artificial Intelligence sem-5 ) 3. What is virtual memory ? My Answer: I was able to explain the concept with great detail and she looked happy with my answer. 4. Explain 4 pillars of OOPS. My Answer: I was prepared for this question. Make sure you prepare for this question with detail and real life examples. 5. Explain primary key and foreign key. My Answer: This looks like an easy question but they expect us to answer it with an example along with the theory. I took 2 tables to explain “customers” and “orders”. And I also explained the foreign key using an SQL statement. 6. Explain API to your Grandmother. My Answer: Firstly, I gave her the definition of the API. I tried explaining using some random examples like Zomato uses Google Maps API.But it was not an appropriate example. I thought again and I came up with an example of a translator. Suppose Person-1 speaks Chinese and Person-2 speaks Marathi and they want to communicate. The translator does the job and acts as an API. She was happy with my answer. 7. Difference between data structure and Algorithm. My Answer: Data structure: container to store data. Algorithm: Procedure to accomplish a task. She further asked me if the algorithm is a process or procedure? I replied with “procedure”. 8. Puzzle: Calculate 45 minutes using 2 uneven ropes. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-1-how-to-measure-45-minutes-using-two-identical-wires/ My Answer: I was unable to solve the question, the key to the puzzle solving is just dont give up. Everyone was asked puzzles and as far as I know no-one was able to solve them, they use puzzles just to check our will to solve a problem and our logical thinking. She gave me ample amount of time and we discussed the solutions I provided and at the end she took me through the correct answer. 9. Do you have any questions for me? My Answer: Don’t take such questions lightly because they want to check how well we are prepared for the interview and our enthusiasm for a position in the company. I asked “How does Deutsche Bank handle global transactions?” 3. Technical Interview 2 [1 hour] Difficulty: Medium The interviewer was a bit serious this time. She jumped straight onto my resume. We had a brief discussion about my internship work for about 5-6 minutes. Then she read my resume line by line and questioned me about everything. We had a discussion about my projects and she asked me how I implement specific functionalities and how I could have done it better. I did my main project in Next Js, so she asked me the difference between Next Js and React Js and why I preferred it over React Js. She grilled me over every tech-stack I wrote in my resume, so be prepared for deep questions on your tech-stack and its internal working too. We discussed my projects for a good amount of 20 minutes in detail. 1. Reverse a linked list. 2. Sort an Array using JavaScript without using Javascript Sort function. My Answer: I explained bubble sort, its working and the time complexity. Then she asked me if better optimal algorithms exist. I replied “Yes” . Merge Sort and Quick sort are much more optimal. Then she asked me why I did not explain these optimal Algorithms. I replied that it was easier to explain Bubble Sort than the recursive algorithms, she smiled at my answer and looked satisfied with my answer. 3. She asked me if I have twitter in my phone, and how tweets are stored, like which data structure can be the most appropriate? My Answer: Obviously I was confused, so I went with the linked list and tried to justify my answer by speaking about allocating memory in non-contiguous fashion. She didn't show any expression on her face and moved onto the next question. 4. Explain Binary Search using a real life example. 5. Derive the time complexity of Binary Search. 6. Explain Inheritance in JavaScript. My Answer: I didn't know the syntax for inheritance in JavaScript so I told her that I have studied OOPS in C++ and explained inheritance using C++. The tech round 2 was mostly based on my resume. So make sure you are thorough with your resume and write only those things which you know properly. 4. Professional Fitness [45 min] Difficulty: Medium This round was scheduled after the lunch break, the interviewer asked me if I had food and what I ate. I said chole bhature then he was enthusiastic all of a sudden. We spoke about the quality of the canteen. He then started with the typical “introduce yourself” question. He asked me about my internship work. 1. List all the sorting algorithms you know, compare the time complexities. 2. Write the code for Quick Sort. 3. Give a real life example for bubble sort. 4. What is recursion? Explain it with a real world example. 5. How is the data actually stored in a computer? How is data inside an array and data inside a linked list stored? 6. Suppose I give you 50 lakh rs right now how would you develop your website? [system Design] 7. He asked me about the apps on my phone. I said Instagram, Twitter etc. He then asked me how instagram works? (PS- He just wanted to check if I am curious to learn the internal working of things) 8. Explain cloud and its services. 9. Where is the Headquarters of Deutsche Bank? 10. Why do you want to work with Deutsche Bank? This was the most challenging round for me as there was a lot of variation in the questions. And I was not much aware about cloud computing and system design, so I tried my best to answer the questions without directly saying “I don't know”. 5. HR Interview [20 min] 1. Introduce Yourself. 2. Interning in the industry is more challenging than in the campus itself. How did interning in VJTI help you? 3. We spoke about sports because my resume mentioned that I’m a part of VJTI Volleyball Team. So he asked why didn't you choose sports as a full time career option? 4. What do you do on weekends? My Answer: Outdoors I like playing Volleyball. Indoors, I like playing FIFA on PC and I like watching web series. So he asked which was the most recent webseries i have watched? Peaky Blinder I said instantly he smiled at my answer. 5. Do you have any plans to study abroad? 6. Describe yourself in one word. 7. Suppose you are working in a team and your teammates aren’t working. What will you do about it? 8. Why do you want to join Deutsche Bank? 9. Do you have any questions for me? The final results were announced at about 9 pm, 26 people were selected and I was fortunate to be one of them. Tips Personal Note: Don't worry if you don't get selected, just keep trying for other opportunities. I personally got rejected by Deutsche Bank (Internship) in the first round itself. Make sure you learn from your failures and always try to get better. Even after not getting a campus internship, preparing well for placements pays off.
